title: What Great Employers Do in a New Hire's First Week
description: The first week shapes whether new employees stay. Here is a simple, repeatable first-week plan that improves ramp-up and retention.
author: Career Education Institute Curriculum Team
coverAlt: Abstract illustration of a checklist in navy, teal and gold
body:
New hires form opinions fast. A chaotic first week sends the message that nobody planned for them. A structured one tells them they made the right choice. Here is what consistently works.

## Before day one
Send a short welcome message with the start time, where to park, what to wear and who will meet them. Have equipment, accounts and safety gear ready. Assign a buddy.

## Day one: belonging and safety
- Introduce the team and the buddy.
- Tour the workplace, including exits, first aid and how to report hazards.
- Complete required paperwork, including Form I-9.
- Review the job description and the 30-60-90 day plan.
- Give them one real task they can finish.

## Days two to four: foundations
Every new hire in the same role should learn the same fundamentals: what the job involves, the vocabulary, the core procedures and the safety rules. Self-paced role training handles the basics consistently, so supervisors can focus on your equipment and processes. Pair it with shadowing an experienced employee.

## Day five: first check-in
Ask three questions: What is going well? What is confusing? What do you need from me? Fix what you can right away.

## Keep it going
Schedule check-ins at 30, 60 and 90 days and use competency sign-offs so everyone knows what “ready” means.
